title: libcurl.dll memory growth during repeated multithreaded downloads on Windows
body: I see memory consumption continually increase while using libcurl.dll 8.4.0 on Windows. My Visual Studio test repeatedly downloads a file in an endless loop, splitting it across 64 threads; after 15–30 minutes, memory usage grows many times over. I linked a test project. If I am failing to release curl resources promptly, I would like to know the correct cleanup.

symptoms_visible: While my program repeatedly downloads a file through libcurl.dll using 64 threads, Windows shows its memory consumption growing many times over after 15–30 minutes.
N0.label: N0 repeated-download memory growth reported

symptoms_visible: I see the process memory increase after each file download in Windows Task Manager, and it does not return to its starting level.
My write callback only counts or discards the received bytes; it does not save the downloaded data.
N1.label: N1 memory observation and DLL lifecycle clarified

symptoms_visible: In the simplified one-thread loop, memory rises from about 1.6 MB to 6.7 MB after 1000 downloads and to about 12 MB after 2000 downloads, even though every easy handle is cleaned up.
Commenting out curl_easy_perform stops the increase, while setting CURLOPT_BUFFERSIZE to 5000 does not change it.
N2.label: N2 simplified reproducer scales with completed transfers

symptoms_visible: The repeated-download memory increase occurs with my 7.82 and 8.4 DLLs, but not with 7.45 or 7.69.
A DLL I build with static SSL support shows the increase; otherwise the same build without SSL support stays stable.
N3.label: N3 growth isolated to the static OpenSSL build

symptoms_visible: After rebuilding with a wrapper that performs the TLS cleanup for each terminating worker thread, I no longer see memory continually increase during repeated downloads.
N_terminal.label: terminal per-thread OpenSSL cleanup verified

question_patterns: What memory measurement are you watching, and how does it change between downloads?
Can you quantify the growth and say which tool reports it?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I cannot identify the allocations inside the external DLL with the Visual Studio debugger. I am watching Windows Task Manager: memory grows after each file download and does not return to its starting level.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The memory rises only during a transfer and always returns to the original level once that transfer finishes.
I see the same per-download increase in Process Explorer instead of Task Manager.

question_patterns: How often do you load and unload the DLL during the loop?
Are you repeatedly calling LoadLibrary, or is libcurl.dll loaded once for the process?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I load libcurl.dll once at program startup. The loop repeatedly creates downloads; it is not repeatedly loading a new copy of the DLL.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I actually call LoadLibrary for every download and never balance those calls with FreeLibrary.

edges.comment: Reporter evidence from c4-c8: the reporter's Windows process is measured through Task Manager, the DLL is loaded once, and the callback discards data. No setup or result from the other participants is folded into the reporter's system.

question_patterns: Can you reduce this to a single-thread loop based on the simple libcurl example and report the memory numbers?
Please test repeated single transfers with curl_easy_init, curl_easy_perform and curl_easy_cleanup in one worker at a time.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I made a one-thread test that downloads a 1.3 MB file repeatedly. It calls curl_easy_init, curl_easy_perform and curl_easy_cleanup every time. Memory starts around 1.6 MB and is around 6.7 MB after 1000 downloads.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: In the single-thread test, memory rises initially but plateaus and stays at the same level through 1000 downloads.
The same test grows from about 2 MB to 7 MB after 1000 downloads.

question_patterns: Does the memory still increase if the loop creates and cleans up easy handles without performing the request?
Can you test whether the increase depends on curl_easy_perform actually running?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: If I comment out the curl_easy_perform line, I do not see the memory increase.

question_patterns: Does the growth continue proportionally if you run 2000 downloads instead of 1000?
Please run the simplified loop longer and report whether it plateaus or continues increasing.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It does not plateau in that test. I start around 1.5 MB, reach about 6.6 MB after 1000 laps, and about 12 MB after 2000 laps.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It remains around 6.6 MB from lap 1000 through lap 2000.

question_patterns: Does changing the transfer buffer size alter the observed growth?
What happens if you repeat the test with a much smaller CURLOPT_BUFFERSIZE?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I set CURLOPT_BUFFERSIZE to 5000. It did not affect the result in any way.

edges.comment: Reporter measurements from c10-c14 and c21: the reporter produced the simplified source and raw working-set figures. The buffer-size variation is treated as a measurement probe, not as a solution attempt.

question_patterns: Which exact libcurl builds have you tested with this reduced reproducer?
Can you compare several older and newer DLL versions and list the result for each?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With my DLLs, 8.4 and 7.82 show the memory increase. I do not see it with 7.45 or 7.69.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every build from 7.45 through 8.4 grows by the same amount per transfer.
7.69 is also affected, but 7.45 remains stable.

question_patterns: Which TLS backend and library linkage does the affected DLL use?
Can you rebuild the same DLL with optional components varied one at a time and report which build shows the growth?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I built the DLL myself. With `WITH_ZLIB=static WITH_NGHTTP2=static WITH_SSL=static`, I see the memory increase. With the otherwise similar build using only `WITH_ZLIB=static WITH_NGHTTP2=static`, I do not see it. The SSL library in the affected build is OpenSSL 3.2.0.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The memory increases identically in both builds, including the build without SSL support.
The same linkage-dependent result occurs with a nearby OpenSSL 3.x version rather than 3.2.0.

edges.comment: Reporter evidence from c15, c22 and c27: the reporter rebuilt the DLL and isolated the result to the static OpenSSL configuration. The stable master build in c16 and debug build in c25 belong to other operators and are deliberately not represented as tests on the reporter's system.

solution.intent: Clean up OpenSSL's per-thread state when each short-lived download thread exits. For a Windows libcurl DLL containing statically linked OpenSSL, call OPENSSL_thread_stop through an appropriate wrapper before the worker returns, or perform the equivalent cleanup from the DLL thread-detach path.
solution.concrete_example: Add an internal or exported wrapper that calls `OPENSSL_thread_stop()`, invoke it for each download worker before that thread terminates, and rerun the 1000–2000 transfer loop. A Windows DLL implementation can instead invoke the cleanup on thread detach. The reporter rebuilt curl with such a wrapper and then stopped seeing the continuing memory increase.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied only the build comparison and the result of the cleanup wrapper. Mapping that evidence to OpenSSL thread-local allocations that are not automatically released when OpenSSL is statically linked into this DLL was the maintainer's diagnosis. The important lifecycle boundary is thread termination, not easy-handle destruction.

edges.comment: Technical resolution from c28-c35: participant6 identified the static-OpenSSL thread cleanup requirement; in c29 the reporter rebuilt curl with a wrapper around OPENSSL_thread_stop and confirmed on the reporter's own Windows system that the continuing growth was no longer visible. Later discussion concerned whether curl should perform this internally on DLL thread detach; the reporter's verified custom build, rather than another operator's setup, supplies the terminal observation.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the affected libcurl DLL contains statically linked OpenSSL, whose per-thread state is not being released when the application's short-lived download threads terminate.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: growth scales with completed transfers despite curl_easy_cleanup, disappears when curl_easy_perform is skipped, and occurs in the static-SSL build but not the otherwise similar build without SSL.

Must recommend per-thread OpenSSL cleanup using OPENSSL_thread_stop before each worker exits, or the equivalent Windows DLL thread-detach handling; ordinary curl_easy_cleanup is not sufficient for this thread-local state.
Must not describe this as a version-independent generic libcurl leak: the reporter's own version and build matrix contradicts that claim.
Must not recommend changing CURLOPT_BUFFERSIZE as the fix, since setting it to 5000 did not alter the observed growth.
Must have the reporter rerun the repeated-download loop and observe stable memory before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Windows C/C++ application developer who can use Visual Studio, dynamically load libcurl, modify test programs, build libcurl with nmake, and vary static library options, but initially lacks tools for tracing allocations inside an external DLL.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, persistent, and empirical. Provides source snippets and numeric Task Manager observations, tests requested variants, and challenges library-ownership assumptions when they complicate deployment.
